title: Supplementary Table S16. Characteristics by postoperative AKI evaluability
notes: Binary-variable means are proportions. AKI, acute kidney injury; ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; AUC, area under the deficit curve; SD, standard deviation; SMD, standardised mean difference. Reference AUC per anaesthesia-hour is expressed in mmHg min h-1.

title: Supplementary Table S17. Sequential absolute hidden-burden models for postoperative ICU stay of at least 2 days
notes: Absolute hidden burden was scaled per 10 mmHg min h-1. Primary adjusted models treated four context-incompatible source-recorded ASA=6 values as missing. The final model additionally used a three-degree-of-freedom spline of log(1 + total reference AUC per anaesthesia-hour). Modified Poisson models used subject-cluster robust variance. Analysis-plan-defined stability criteria required convergence, finite positive confidence limits, at least five events per parameter, and a CI width ratio no greater than 10. VitalDB does not distinguish planned from unplanned ICU admission; this is a supplementary resource-use association. ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; ICU, intensive care unit; RR, relative risk. All three models met these numerical stability criteria.

title: Supplementary Table S18. ASA Physical Status data-quality audit
notes: All four source-recorded values outside 1-5 were ASA=6 and were incompatible with the included non-donor operative context. Because the de-identified dataset provided no audit trail for adjudication, no replacement clinical class was assigned and these values were set to missing in primary adjusted models. ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists.

title: Supplementary Table S23. Case-level distributions under a 5 min display
notes: Mean arterial pressure threshold: 65 mmHg. Each case contributes one average across 30 sampling phases. Area ratios require positive reference deficit area; 42 zero-area cases remain in absolute state-discordance summaries. State discordance excludes display-unavailable time. Case summaries are not pooled exposure ratios. Among 1899 cases with ≥60 s episodes, the miss fraction was 36.7% [24.8 to 50.2%], with 5th to 95th percentiles 3.3 to 70.0%; within-case phase range was 66.7 [50.0 to 100.0] percentage points. Aggregate quantiles are in the workbook; case-level trajectories are not redistributed.

The onset carry-in row overlaps with fresh sampling and must not be added to the first three rows. Percentile intervals resample 2380 subjects, retaining all operations (1000 replicates, seed 20260706).

title: Supplementary Table S25. Compact event-definition robustness
notes: Threshold: mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg; 5 min display, 30 phases. Gap allowance joins only finite observed normal-pressure bins, never missing values. Minimum duration is cumulative low-pressure time, excluding normal gaps. Each row defines a different event population, so event counts are not paired comparisons or multiple independent cohorts. The first row reproduces original event counts and display visibility exactly. Subject-bootstrap intervals: 1000 replicates, seed 20260706. Longer events are less often missed; these are measurement results, not treatment effects.

title: Supplementary Table S26. Absolute interval summaries with subject-clustered uncertainty
notes: MAP<65 mmHg; 2435 cases/2380 subjects; 9187 ≥60 s reference events. Counts average every 10 s phase. Low display includes inherited values. Duration/AUC include runs <60 s; TWA uses 532 190.5 valid-reference minutes throughout. Initial unavailable display contributes no displayed burden; missing reference bins are excluded. CIs use 1000 subject resamples: original event draws for percentages, frequency-analysis draws for absolute exposures, and 5 min draws for the reference. They are not between-interval difference CIs. Unrounded estimates, count CIs and 55/60-mmHg summaries are in the workbook. AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure; TWA, time-weighted average.
values: Events with low display, expected n; % (95% CI)

title: Supplementary Table S28. Display information at low-reference adjustments
notes: Low reference denotes MAP below 65 mmHg. Display states use 236 low-reference events in 85 cases from 83 subjects and sum to 100% before rounding. They describe the adjustment instant, not detection at any time during the whole episode reported in Table 3. Recovery persistence is averaged over all 184 events with confirmed recovery (80 cases, 78 subjects), with equal weight per event after averaging all sampling phases. Normal or unavailable display at recovery confirmation contributes 0 min. Persistence is restricted to the remainder of the 5 min post-adjustment window and terminates at normal display, missing reference or recurrent hypotension. CIs use subject-cluster resampling. A normal emulated display was not what the treating team necessarily saw. CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

notes: MAP threshold 65 mmHg, 5 min display. Each rule changes one feature of the primary analysis. One event per subject is selected by case identifier then relative time; chronological surgery order is unavailable. Equal subject weighting first averages events within each subject. These are descriptive sensitivity estimates, not treatment-effect comparisons. CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure.
values: At least 30 s preceding low MAP

title: Supplementary Table S30. Cohort retention under startup signal-quality rules
notes: Startup means the first 600 s after the first finite arterial-reference MAP. A flagged bin has numeric MAP <40 mmHg, waveform coverage >=80%, and a 5th-to-95th percentile waveform span <=5 mmHg. Sustained segments require >=60 s continuously flagged; all flagged bins has no duration requirement. These are rule-based technical sensitivities, without completed clinical adjudication.

Masked time is counted before coverage exclusions. For the first two masking rules, whole-case reference coverage must still be >=80%. The 10 min window sensitivity retains the original cohort. Cases without a source waveform are retained. AUC, area under the deficit curve; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

title: Supplementary Table S31. Bidirectional deficit and event visibility after startup quality checks
notes: MAP <65 mmHg, 5 min display, all 30 phases. Qualifying events require >=60 s of continuous finite low reference pressure. Values in parentheses are 95% subject-cluster percentile confidence intervals (1000 replicates). The last three rows are mutually exclusive and sum to 100% before rounding.

Rules are defined in Table S30. Original global sampling phases and anaesthesia durations are retained. Masked values cannot initialise or update the held display. Missing reference bins break episodes.

title: Supplementary Table S32. Display information at infusion adjustments under startup quality rules
notes: Values in parentheses are 95% subject-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals (2000 replicates). Infusion event definitions, local pre-adjustment support and recovery rules are unchanged. The denominator for display states is the low-reference adjustment count in each column.

Persistence averages all confirmed recovery events after phase averaging. Normal or unavailable display at recovery contributes zero; lack of recovery is not assigned zero. The duration is restricted to the remainder of the 5 min post-adjustment window. Rules are defined in Table S30.
